text:
Marco Chen: quick heads-up — we saw a spike that pushed router queue depth to 95% for ~30s, a bunch of long-running requests piled up and we got cascading timeouts
Priya Rao: ouch. do we have per-key early-shed configured? i thought we only did per-org + global priority so far
Danielle (eng-platform): we have per-key token buckets but they replenish slowly, so when many keys burst concurrently they all hit the global queue and start starving each other
Lina Gomez: proposal: add a priority-decay window so older low-priority requests age out faster and free slots for fresh interactive traffic
Marco Chen: +1 for aging, but we need clear rules: decay should be proportional to queue time and request cost (tokens). otherwise it gets gameable
Priya Rao: also consider emitting an "early-shed" header to clients so SDKs can switch to offline fallback instead of waiting for a retry
Danielle (eng-platform): idea for header: X-Redwood-Shed: reason=priority_decay; retry_after=2; hint=soft_drop. would that work with existing SDKs?
Lina Gomez: yep, SDKs can interpret retry_after < 1 as guidance to degrade locally. we should avoid pretending it's a 429 though if it's an intentional early drop for global overload
Marco Chen: this is the crux: 429 == per-key/quota reject; 503 == global overload. If we early-shed to preserve SLOs, do we return 503 or a synthetic 429?
Priya Rao: my vote: 429 for quota-limited (client is abusive/over limit). 503 for platform-level shedding. But surface a machine-readable header that distinguishes "soft-shed" vs "hard-reject"
Danielle (eng-platform): agree. telemetry on the console should break down rejects by classifier: per-key_quota, per-org_burst, global_backpressure, priority_decay. Those metrics need to be per-route and per-model
Lina Gomez: and add a small sampling of request IDs for shed events to the errors dashboard so we can trace if a user sees progressive degradation after a rollout
Marco Chen: rollout UX: default off for priority-decay. roll out via canary flag + router telemetry, watch shed-rate and latency 95/99. if shed-rate jumps, auto-roll back. deploy-bot can toggle canaries
Priya Rao: for graceful behavior we should implement a tiny backoff-credit header so clients can do adaptive pacing: e.g. X-Redwood-Backoff-Credit: "+0.5" or "-1.0" to indicate tokens gained/lost
Danielle (eng-platform): example config snippet for the router (pseudo):
```
route: /v1/chat
burst_window_ms: 1000
priority_decay_ms: 12000
early_shed_threshold: 0.85
shedding_policy:
  - type: priority_decay
    weight_by_tokens: true
  - type: global_capacity
    fallback_status: 503
headers:
  emit_backoff_credit: true
```
Lina Gomez: need to be careful with headers and caching/CDN — ensure we don't leak per-key state to downstream caches. set Cache-Control: private for shed responses
Priya Rao: and telemetry: expose per-tenancy "effective_shed_rate" in the Console (heatmap), plus a time series of average queue-time, and a histogram of shed reasons
Marco Chen: ops playbook: if global_backpressure > 1% sustained for 5m, escalate to oncall. simple alerts: shed-rate, rising queue depth, drop in throughput
Danielle (eng-platform): can someone own a small spike experiment? implement priority-decay code + headers, feature flag behind canary, add console panels + sampling. I'll wire up the router side if someone does the console/SDK bits
Lina Gomez: I can add the Console panels and sampling UI, also add the shed reason breakdown on the route page
Priya Rao: I'll update SDKs to handle X-Redwood-Shed and X-Redwood-Backoff-Credit, plus a local degrade mode tied to retry_after < 1
Marco Chen: great — owners: Danielle (router), Lina (console), Priya (SDK). I'll create the canary job + deploy toggle with deploy-bot. keep the initial flag default off for production
sre-bot: incident-note: 1923456789-1 - transient queue overload at 2026-07-12T14:33:09Z; root cause under investigation; next update in #incidents
Marco Chen: thanks, will follow up with a PR for the router config later today
Priya Rao: quick question — do we want to surface a per-user "shed_reason" in the usage API so support can tell customers why requests were dropped?
Danielle (eng-platform): yes but redact identifying tokens, only provide reason + sample request_id + timestamp to support console
Lina Gomez: sounds good. putting the dashboard cards on my board for this week
Marco Chen: ok closing thread for now, we'll post progress updates in this channel. :thumbsup:
